newsitem.title: NORWAY: FOCUS - Aker RGI posts H1 operating loss.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Aker RGI posts H1 operating loss.

text.p: Norwegian holding company Aker RGI ASA reported a first-half operating loss on Thursday, despite a 26 percent rise in revenues, as restructuring costs resulted in provisions of 520 million crowns ($68.5 million).
The Oslo-based company posted an operating loss of 237 million crowns in the first six month 1997 compared with a profit of 288 million crowns a year ago.
The slump was mainly attributable to heavy provisions at two of the company's three core subsidiaries -- offshore group Aker Maritime ASA and fully integrated fishing group Norway Seafoods ASA.
Group revenues for the period amounted to 12 billion crowns versus 9.51 billion.

Aker RGI, which has interests in the offshore sector, fishing, construction, real estate and shipbuilding, was established last year after Resource Group International (RGI) merged with engineering and construction group Aker ASA.
The operating result did not include a contribution from Aker RGI's 33 percent stake in Swedish/Norwegian building materials group Scancem AB, which is scheduled to post results on August 26.
But Aker RGI's net profit up to June 30 of 308 million crowns included an estimated 80 million crowns contribution from Scancem.
Aker RGI booked a first-half operating result of 96 million crowns from its 75.1 percent owned Aker Maritime, against 151 million crowns in the corresponding year-ago period.

It said earnings at the oil and gas technology company were increasing in most parts of the business, but a provision of 120 million crowns in connection with the North Sea Njord oil platform had a negative impact on operating profits for the period.
The Norway Seafoods division, 60.7 percent owned, took a 400 million crown provision in the first half for restructuring costs.

The group, the world's largest catcher and processor of white fish, booked 250 million crowns as ordinary operating expenses and 150 million crowns as extraordinary costs. Aker RGI posted an operating loss for Norway Seafoods of 129 million crowns versus a 58 million crowns profit a year ago.
"Substantial investment has been made over the past few months in Aker RGI's three core business areas," the company said in a statement.

"Three new boats were acquired in the fishing sector in July, while Aker Maritime has now completed about a third of the company acquisitions required to meet its growth targets up to 2000. Scancem has expanded in Asia through investments in India and Bangladesh."
It added that it continued to focus its business through the sale of interests outside existing core areas and had sold assets worth roughly 3.7 billion crowns since last November.
